name: Buyid Dynasts Seize Baghdad
summary: The Buyid (Buwayhid) amir Muizz al-Dawla enters Baghdad and effectively deposes the Abbasid Caliph al-Mustakfi, replacing him with a puppet and taking the title Amir al-Umara (Commander of Commanders). The Buyids are Shia Muslims controlling a Sunni Abbasid caliph, they keep the caliphate as a source of symbolic legitimacy while exercising real political power. The arrangement lasts until the Seljuk conquest of Baghdad (1055).

_quarry.structural_significance: The Buyid seizure demonstrates that the Abbasid caliphate has become a purely symbolic institution; the pattern of dynasties maintaining a figurehead caliph while exercising real power persists until the Mongol destruction of Baghdad (1258); Buyid patronage of philosophy and Shia scholarship creates a flourishing intellectual culture in Baghdad and western Persia
